h1: Federal Pacific Panel Replacement in Broward County
intro: If you are here, an inspector or an insurance company probably said the words Federal Pacific, or the panel reads FPE or Stab-Lok, and now you are trying to understand what it means. Here is the plain truth, stated once. Federal Pacific panels are widely documented for breakers that may fail to trip when there is a fault, which means the device meant to protect your home might not do its job. That is why carriers refuse to cover homes that have them and why 4-point inspections fail them. Replacing Federal Pacific and Zinsco panels is routine work for us, among the most common jobs we do. We are not alarmed to find one, and you do not need to be either. We come out, confirm the panel in person, and replace it with modern, insurable equipment.

definition.heading: What a Federal Pacific panel is
definition.body: Federal Pacific Electric, often shortened to FPE, is a brand of electrical panel installed in a great many homes built decades ago. The breakers are commonly branded Stab-Lok. Your panel is where power from the utility is split into the circuits that feed your home, and the breakers are the safety devices that are supposed to cut power the moment something goes wrong. The concern with Federal Pacific is well documented and specific. The Stab-Lok breakers may fail to trip under a fault, so the one part of the system whose entire purpose is protection can fall short at the exact moment it is needed. Because the brand is obsolete and the concern is in the design itself, a genuine repair is not practical, and replacement is the honest path. Insurance carriers in South Florida know the name, which is why most owners learn they have one from a renewal notice or a 4-point inspection.

symptoms.title: The panel reads Federal Pacific or FPE
symptoms.body: The clearest sign is the label. If the panel says Federal Pacific or FPE, or the breakers read Stab-Lok, that alone is reason for a licensed look. With this brand it is the name, not a symptom, that carriers and inspectors react to first.

symptoms.title: Your insurer or 4-point flagged it
symptoms.body: A renewal notice or a 4-point inspection named the panel and will not pass the home. This is how most owners find out. The carrier is reacting to the brand's documented history, and the policy stays on hold until the panel is replaced.

symptoms.title: A breaker that will not trip or reset
symptoms.body: A breaker that clearly should have tripped and did not, or one that will not hold a reset, is the exact failure this brand is known for. That is the safety concern in plain terms, and it calls for attention rather than another reset.

symptoms.title: Warmth, buzzing, or a burning smell
symptoms.body: The panel feels warm, hums, or gives off a burning smell. Electricity is something we do not see, we only feel the effect. On an aging Federal Pacific panel, those effects are worth taking seriously and having looked at soon.

symptoms.title: Scorching or melting at the breakers
symptoms.body: You notice browning, melting, or scorch marks where the breakers seat into the panel. That is heat and damage at the connection point, a clear sign the equipment has reached the end of its service life and should be replaced.

symptoms.title: Stab-Lok breakers in an older home
symptoms.body: Panels of a certain age often hold Stab-Lok breakers that push straight onto the bus. If that description fits what you see, have it identified by a licensed electrician. Knowing for certain is the first calm step toward getting the home insurable.

localSections.heading: Why Federal Pacific panels turn up so often here
localSections.body: Federal Pacific panels went into an enormous number of homes during a long building stretch of the last century, and Broward County grew fast in exactly that era. That timing is why the brand shows up again and again when we open panels from West Palm Beach down to North Miami Beach. A home can change hands several times over the decades with the same FPE panel still on the wall, untouched because nothing obvious ever went wrong. Nothing obvious going wrong is not the same as safe with this brand, and that is the heart of the matter. Finding a Federal Pacific panel does not make your home unusual, it makes it typical of when it was built. When we tell an owner they have one, we are rarely surprised to see it, and you do not need to feel singled out. It is simply part of owning a South Florida home from a certain period, and it has a clean, well-understood fix.

localSections.heading: Heat and salt air on aging equipment
localSections.body: A Federal Pacific panel that has spent decades in the South Florida climate has been through a lot. Steady heat keeps the components warm, humidity works into the enclosure, and homes nearer the coast face salt air that slowly corrodes the bus and the terminations where the Stab-Lok breakers seat. A loosened or corroded connection runs hotter than it should, and on equipment already known for trouble, that added heat speeds the wear along. This is why an old FPE panel down here can be in rougher shape inside than the front cover suggests. When we assess one, the condition of the bus and the breaker contacts tells us a great deal about what the job really involves. We build the real environment into the forecast, so the replacement we quote is made to hold up in the heat and humidity it has to live in, not just to look right on the day we finish.

localSections.heading: Permitting and code reality in Broward
localSections.body: Replacing a Federal Pacific panel in Broward County is permitted work, and that protects you. The permit puts a licensed contractor and a county inspector between you and a mistake, and it creates the documentation your insurance carrier will expect to see. Electrical code advances on a multi-year cycle, so the panel we install is built to the current standard, not the one in force when the FPE panel first went up. We pull the permit, schedule the inspection, and we meet the inspector on site in person. That matters when the entire purpose of the job is to satisfy a carrier. The team that priced your replacement and knows every detail of it is standing there when Broward County signs off, so the paperwork that protects your policy is handled fully and correctly, with nothing left half done or open to question later.

localSections.heading: How carriers treat the Federal Pacific name
localSections.body: South Florida insurance carriers know the Federal Pacific name, and many act on it directly. A 4-point inspection that identifies FPE or Stab-Lok equipment can be enough for a carrier to decline a new policy or drop a renewal, even on a home that never gave you a moment of electrical trouble. This is honest, verifiable reality, and it explains why an owner who felt fine about the panel suddenly faces a deadline. We describe it plainly and without drama because it does not need dramatizing. The way forward is clear and we have taken many owners down it. Replace the obsolete panel with modern, code-compliant equipment, pass the county inspection, and the specific objection attached to the Federal Pacific name is removed. From there your policy can proceed on the strength of a service the carrier has no reason to question, which is exactly where you want to be.

guide.title: The complete guide to Federal Pacific panel replacement in South Florida

sections.heading: What a Federal Pacific panel is and why it matters
sections.body: Federal Pacific Electric, usually shortened to FPE, is a brand of electrical panel installed widely in homes built decades ago, including a great many across Broward County. The breakers are commonly labeled Stab-Lok. Your panel is where power from the utility is divided into the circuits that run your home, and the breakers are the safety devices meant to cut power the instant something goes wrong. The concern with Federal Pacific is well documented, and we will state it once, plainly. The Stab-Lok breakers may fail to trip under a fault. That means the one part of your electrical system whose whole purpose is to protect you in a dangerous moment can fall short at the exact time you need it most. That is the issue, and it is enough on its own. We do not need to exaggerate it or frighten you with it. It simply tells us this equipment has reached the end of its trustworthy life, and the honest answer is to replace it with something you can rely on.

sections.heading: Why replacement, not repair, is the honest answer
sections.body: Owners often ask whether a Federal Pacific panel can just be repaired, which is a reasonable question. The honest answer is almost always no. The brand is obsolete, so genuine parts are hard to come by, and the concern is not one failed piece you can swap out. It lives in the design of the Stab-Lok breakers and the way they seat onto the bus, which is the core of the panel itself. Replacing a single breaker does not address why carriers and inspectors react to the whole unit. Spending money to keep an obsolete panel going is money better spent on a modern one that removes the problem for good and satisfies your insurance company in the process. We would rather give you that straight than sell you a repair that leaves the real concern sitting on your wall. Price it once, price it right, and put the issue behind you. That approach costs less worry and, over time, less money too.

sections.heading: When replacement becomes urgent
sections.body: For many owners a Federal Pacific panel sits quietly for years, and the push to replace it arrives from outside the home. The most common trigger in South Florida is insurance. A 4-point inspection identifies the FPE or Stab-Lok equipment, and the carrier says the policy will not renew until the panel is replaced, often with a deadline attached to the renewal. The second trigger is something we can see during an assessment. Scorching where the breakers seat, a breaker that will not trip or hold, or heat damage on the bus moves replacement from a good idea to the clear recommendation. The third trigger is peace of mind. Once an owner understands what the brand is, many simply decide they do not want to keep trusting their family's safety to equipment that may not perform. Any of those reasons is valid. We will tell you honestly which one applies to you, and we will never manufacture urgency that the panel in front of us does not actually warrant. When the only pressure is a carrier's renewal deadline and the panel is otherwise stable, we will give you an honest read on the timing, so you can plan the work around your budget rather than feeling stampeded into it. A genuine deadline deserves a straight answer, never a scare.

sections.heading: What the day of the work looks like
sections.body: Replacing a Federal Pacific panel is focused, familiar work for our crew, because it is among the most common jobs we do. It is an in and out type of situation. That is what we do. We coordinate with the utility so the power feeding the property can be interrupted safely for the work window. Then our in-house crew removes the FPE panel, installs modern equipment in its place, and reconnects every circuit, labeling as we go so you end up with a panel you can actually read. We check and correct the grounding and the connections, because a new panel is only as good as what feeds it. You will be without power for part of the day, and we tell you honestly ahead of time so you can plan around it. Because the same crew does this constantly, the work has a rhythm to it and the property is left clean. When we finish, we schedule the county inspection so your carrier receives the documentation it needs. There is very little you need to do before we arrive, beyond making some room around the panel and planning for a few hours without power. If anyone in the home works remotely or relies on medical equipment, let us know when we schedule so we can set the window around that. We would rather shape the day around your household than ask your household to bend around us. That kind of care is part of giving a customer more than they pay for.

sections.heading: An honest conversation about cost
sections.body: A Federal Pacific panel replacement is quoted per property after an on-site assessment, and we do not post a flat number for a good reason. What the job takes depends on the condition of the existing service, the grounding, the size the property needs, and what we find when we open things up. Two homes with the same FPE panel can hold very different jobs behind the cover. Our service call is $240, which covers roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and diagnosis, and if the problem can be handled on the spot there is no separate return charge. For the replacement itself, we forecast what the job actually takes and give you one price before we begin, and that price does not change mid-job. We do not tack on fees partway through. Price it once, price it right. If a lower bid from someone else looks appealing, ask what it leaves out. Losing an honestly priced job is fine with us. Winning one and padding it later is not something we do.

sections.heading: How to choose the right contractor for this work
sections.body: Because a panel sits at the center of your home's safety, and the reason for this job is usually your insurance, the contractor you pick matters as much as the equipment going in. Start with licensing. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor with statewide authority and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Ask whether the contractor can pull the permit in their own name and who attends the inspection, because when the team that priced the job meets the inspector, the documentation your carrier needs gets handled correctly. Ask who actually performs the work. An in-house crew that replaces these panels routinely is a different thing from a rotating set of subcontractors seeing one for the first time. And be cautious of anyone who sells by tearing down every other company or inventing urgency. We do not work that way. We state the concern with Federal Pacific once, we let our license and our record speak for us, and we give a customer more than what they pay for. A contractor worth hiring should also be able to explain the Federal Pacific concern in plain terms, without shrugging it off and without leaning on fear to push a sale. If someone cannot calmly tell you why the brand is a problem and what replacement actually fixes, take note of that. We are glad to show you what we see inside your panel, explain why we recommend what we do, and then let you decide in your own time and on your own terms.

sections.heading: After the replacement: what changes
sections.body: Once the Federal Pacific panel is gone and modern equipment stands in its place, several real things change for you. The insurance objection tied to the brand is removed, so your policy can proceed on a service the carrier has no reason to question, and the 4-point item that failed now passes cleanly. The breakers protecting your home will trip when they are supposed to, which is the whole reason they exist. Proper grounding and solid connections keep the heart of your electrical system running cool and quiet. Grounding is not a gimmick and we never frame it as more than it is. It protects your family, your home, and your investment as a whole, and it is simply part of doing the job right. On top of all that, you get to stop thinking about the panel at all, which carries its own quiet value. We show up when we say we will, we replace the equipment properly, and then it works, steadily, in the background, the way it always should have. If your insurance paperwork needs the permit details or the inspection record, we make sure you leave with everything your carrier asks for, so getting covered again goes as smoothly as the work did. We do not count the job as finished until you are insured and at ease.
